column1: # Game profile of Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door (Switch, update 1.0.1 = v65536). Plays on the Mac at 60 fps (title, a new file, the prologue and the opening into Rogueport, with sound)

# Intelligent Systems' engine on NintendoWare (G3d, Vfx, Atk), NVN, SDK 15.3.2 (the sdk build of Celeste). Nearly every RomFS file is zstd (named .zst), the event scripts and data tables are ELF files
# the engine reads as data, and the movies are WebM (VP9 + Vorbis) through the SDK's movie library (subsdk0).
# The shaders are BNSH: 8,993 in shaders/*.bfsha.zst and 2,865 in the particle effects (effect/particle/*.ptcl.zst); shaders/tessellation.bfsha holds 4 domain shaders, which the host does not run

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# only the merged 1.0.1 copy is extracted
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk (subsdk0 = NintendoSDK_movie)
# The NPDM declares 8 MB of system resource (virtual address memory), and main never calls SetMemoryHeapSize. nninitStartup (main+0x3136b8) makes the game's malloc a StandardAllocator over
# 62 GB of address space, which patches.py cuts to 4 GB, and cuts its 256 MB, 16 MB and 1 MB allocators out of it. With the sdk cuts (node area 62 MB, 32 MB alignment for large regions)
# the region spans alias +62 MB to +4.06 GB of Engage's 5 GB block (256 MB in front + 4.375 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 128 MB heap region, never used). The allocator maps 1.5 GB
# at boot and 2.0 GB by the arrival in Rogueport, under the hardware pool
# the NPDM declares 8 MB of system resource
# The D-pad opens the Gear and Journal menus (the HUD shows it in Rogueport): the iPhone pad starts in the 3D layout, which has one
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch). The game asks for present interval 2 (a value fixed at startup) and steps its clocks by the 60 Hz vsyncs it measures between frames, at least 2. Two
# changes on 1.0.1's main (patches.py): the floor goes down to 1, and the base clock takes the host's frame step (FRAME_STEP), the vsyncs each frame stays on screen: 1 at 60 fps,
# 2 when 60 does not hold, so game time = real time. Fades take the same time at 60 fps as at 30 (Mac, the same press script). DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone)
# Late frames are shown as soon as they are ready, not held longer: the game's frame waits for its three render workers (gfx::ParallelManager), and holding frames left them idle,
# so the cost of a frame grew with the hold (1.4 vsyncs at hold 1, 3.3 at hold 2 on a loaded Mac) and the hold stuck at 3 vsyncs, 20 fps; without holds the same load gave
# 32-58 fps at 0.994 of real time. DM_FPS_HOLD=on brings the holds back
# ---- Shader split (shader_split.py: BNSH in the zstd .bfsha and .ptcl files) ----
